chunks: And Hārūn ibn Muslim narrated from Mas‘adah ibn Ṣadaqah al-Raba‘ī, from Ja‘far ibn Muḥammad, from his father عليه السلام:

That a man from the Anṣār passed away, and he had young children, and he had six slaves. So he freed them at the time of his death, and he had no property other than them. Then the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم was approached and informed, so he said:
What did you do with your companion?
They said: We buried him. He said:
Had I known, I would not have had him buried among the people of Islam. He left his children begging from the people.

key_terms.الرَّقِيقِ: slaves or bondsmen owned as property
key_terms.صِبْيَةٌ صِغَارٌ: young children left behind by the deceased
key_terms.عِنْدَ مَوْتِهِ: at the time of his death
key_terms.فَأَعْتَقَهُمْ: he manumitted them and set them free

ai.seo_question: Can a dying person give away all his property if he leaves behind needy young children?
ai.summary: This hadith relates that a man freed all his slaves at death despite having no other wealth and leaving behind young children. The Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم strongly condemned this because it neglected the rights and welfare of his dependents, showing that disposal of one's estate must remain within what is proper and just.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications:
Hadith.5427 - Harun ibn Muslim narrated from Masadah ibn Ṣadaqah Al-Rabii from Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq (as) from his father, Imam Muhammad ibn Ali Al-Baqir (as), who said:
"A man from the Ansar passed away, leaving behind young children.
He had six slaves and no wealth other than them. At the time of his death, he freed all of them.

When the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) was informed of this, He (sw) said:
'What did you do with your companion?'
They replied: 'We buried him.'
Prophet (sw) said: 'Had I known before, I would not have allowed him to be buried among the Muslims. He (the deceased) left his children to beg from the people.'"
